changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The newly delivered independent validation resolves the main MSI-high comparison in favor of a strong, scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency association. H81 has discovery signed estimate +0.775 [0.664, 0.885] and independent validation signed estimate +0.842 [0.673, 1.010]; both are far above the 0.15 composite-unit threshold in the claimed direction and mutually consistent. Combined with the already supported conditional and technical strata—including the triple-intact TP53-/KEAP1-/SMARCA4-intact stratum, adenocarcinoma, batch_a, Avana library, median-or-higher screen quality, elevated mutation burden, and high Cas9 activity strata—the MSI-high association is well established as a dataset-level predictor of lower composite scores. I therefore accept H81 and close it as a completed main robustness claim. The new PTEN batch_a validation does not resolve that subgroup claim. Discovery for H94 was +0.258 [0.063, 0.454], while independent validation was +0.190 [-0.061, 0.440]. The validation point estimate remains directionally positive, but the interval crosses both null and the threshold, so the batch_a-specific PTEN association remains unsupported as a standalone claim. This should not be interpreted as evidence against the broader PTEN association, which remains accepted primarily on the basis of the overall PTEN comparison and the independently validated triple-intact stratum. The current supplied-dataset scientific summary is: TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency, signed main effect +0.829 [0.767, 0.891]; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency, signed main effect +0.810 [0.745, 0.875] and validated +0.788 [0.698, 0.879]; SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency, signed main effect +0.804 [0.742, 0.867] and validated +0.800 [0.705, 0.895]; MSI-high status is associated with much stronger dependency, now validated +0.842 [0.673, 1.010]; and PTEN loss has a moderate stronger-dependency association, best supported in the triple-intact TP53-/KEAP1-/SMARCA4-intact stratum, discovery +0.252 [0.169, 0.335] and validation +0.281 [0.159, 0.403], while several direct subgroup estimates remain imprecise. Negative or unsupported findings remain important: STK11 loss, KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, MTAP loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, PIK3CA mutation, APC mutation, NF1 loss, media serum percentage, and the three research markers D/E/F show no meaningful association, and ERBB2 amplification and BRAF V600E are near-null. EGFR amplification produced only a weak opposite-direction signal and remains unsupported as a stronger-dependency predictor. Most interaction tests involving the accepted predictors do not support meaningful multiplicative heterogeneity. The next most informative step is to register a stricter PTEN refinement excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status, because this tests whether the moderate PTEN association persists when both the largest genomic co-occurrence effects and the strong MSI-high effect are excluded. I also prioritize the already registered direct technical robustness checks for TP53 and KEAP1 in high screen-quality and high Cas9-activity strata, SMARCA4 in elevated mutation burden, and the Ky-library main-effect technical scale check. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset; they are not causal single-gene knockout effects or claims of external biological generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The strongest supplied-dataset associations are now well replicated: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associate with higher composite scores, meaning weaker dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high associate with more negative scores, meaning stronger dependency. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency predictor but is close to the 0.15-unit threshold in several strata. The next exploration should therefore test whether these associations remain meaningful in states that could plausibly confound or modify them, especially chromosomal instability/aneuploidy, EMT/stress programs, screen batch or library scale, and co-occurring large predictor states. I register direct mean-difference estimates for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, and PTEN loss within the top quartile of aneuploidy_score. If these signed effects remain above threshold, the large predictor associations are less likely to be artifacts of genome-wide instability or aneuploidy-associated proliferation. For PTEN specifically, I register a stricter clean-stratum comparison: PTEN loss among samples intact for TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 and with median-or-higher Cas9 activity score. This tests both independence from the largest genomic co-occurrence effects and preservation under better editing activity. I also register state-specific robustness checks for TP53 loss in high EMT and KEAP1 loss in high hypoxia, since EMT and stress programs may alter composite scores. Finally, I register a CRISPR-library Avana main-effect technical scale check and a CDKN2A-loss comparison among samples intact for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI; this tests whether the near-threshold CDKN2A signal survives after removing the strongest known predictors and MSI-high status. All proposed claims are associations in the supplied dataset, not causal single-gene knockout effects or externally generalizable biological conclusions.

prompt:
Iteration 8/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The next exploration should therefore test whether these associations remain meaningful in states that could plausibly confound or modify them, especially chromosomal instability/aneuploidy, EMT/stress programs, screen batch or library scale, and co-occurring large predictor states. I register direct mean-difference estimates for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, and PTEN loss within the top quartile of aneuploidy_score. If these signed effects remain above threshold, the large predictor associations are less likely to be artifacts of genome-wide instability or aneuploidy-associated proliferation. For PTEN specifically, I register a stricter clean-stratum comparison: PTEN loss among samples intact for TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 and with median-or-higher Cas9 activity score. This tests both independence from the largest genomic co-occurrence effects and preservation under better editing activity. I also register state-specific robustness checks for TP53 loss in high EMT and KEAP1 loss in high hypoxia, since EMT and stress programs may alter composite scores. Finally, I register a CRISPR-library Avana main-effect technical scale check and a CDKN2A-loss comparison among samples intact for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI; this tests whether the near-threshold CDKN2A signal survives after removing the strongest known predictors and MSI-high status. These are important because accepted effects and interactions should remain interpretable across screen batches; direct stratum estimates can determine whether large accepted associations survive in an actual batch stratum, whereas many batch interactions were only deferred or indirect. Second, H85, H91, and H102 test MSI-high robustness in the dominant Avana library, median-or-better screen-quality strata, and elevated mutation-burden strata. The latter is especially informative because MSI status is correlated with genome-wide mutation burden; a preserved strong MSI-high effect under elevated burden would argue that MSI-high is not merely proxying mutation burden. Third, H100 and H101 test SMARCA4 and MSI-high effects in median-or-higher Cas9 activity strata, addressing a possible technical dependence on editing activity for the strongest new dependencies. All three intervals lie far above the 0.15-unit threshold in the claimed direction. Iteration 8/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The twelve new discovery analyses strongly reinforce the accepted large predictor associations and clarify which technical or biological strata are decisive. TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in both median-or-better screen-quality samples (+0.838 [0.753,0.923]) and median-or-higher Cas9-activity samples (+0.753 [0.659,0.847]). KEAP1 loss likewise remains associated with weaker dependency in high screen-quality samples (+0.772 [0.678,0.866]) and high Cas9-activity samples (+0.711 [0.612,0.810]). SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in elevated mutation-burden samples (+0.847 [0.755,0.939]). Together with earlier batch, library, lineage, Cas9, screen-quality, and mutation-burden checks, these results argue that the largest associations are not artifacts of screen quality, editing activity, mutation burden, or screen batch. High aneuploidy robustness checks are also strong: TP53 loss +0.891 [0.768,1.013], KEAP1 loss +0.875 [0.736,1.015], SMARCA4 loss +0.784 [0.652,0.916], and MSI-high +0.892 [0.669,1.114], although the MSI-high exposed cell is small. Thus, these accepted associations survive the top quartile of genome-wide chromosomal instability. For PTEN loss, the clean quadruple-intact stratum excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high gives +0.260 [0.182,0.338], entirely above the 0.15-unit threshold and the strongest direct PTEN robustness estimate to date. I accept it and request validation because PTEN is the moderate predictor closest to threshold and this stratum removes the largest competing predictors. In contrast, PTEN loss in the triple-intact high-Cas9 stratum is directionally supportive (+0.204 [0.092,0.316]) but imprecise, with lower bound below threshold; it remains unresolved and is deferred rather than validated separately. The Ky-library main-effect check is not supportive of the claimed positive technical shift: signed estimate -0.061 [-0.129,0.008], so that claimed positive library effect is rejected. All conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal or externally generalizable biological claims.

prompt:
Iteration 8/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Interpret all findings as supplied-dataset associations only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The strongest supplied-dataset associations are now well replicated: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associate with higher composite scores, meaning weaker dependency, whereas SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high associate with more negative scores, meaning stronger dependency. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency predictor but is close to the 0.15-unit threshold in several strata. The next exploration should therefore test whether these associations remain meaningful in states that could plausibly confound or modify them, especially chromosomal instability/aneuploidy, EMT/stress programs, screen batch or library scale, and co-occurring large predictor states. I register direct mean-difference estimates for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, and PTEN loss within the top quartile of aneuploidy_score. If these signed effects remain above threshold, the large predictor associations are less likely to be artifacts of genome-wide instability or aneuploidy-associated proliferation. For PTEN specifically, I register a stricter clean-stratum comparison: PTEN loss among samples intact for TP53, KEAP1, and SMARCA4 and with median-or-higher Cas9 activity score. record.narrative: The newly delivered validation and interaction tests substantially consolidate the current scientific picture as a set of supplied-dataset associations, not causal effects or externally generalizable biology. H108 is the most consequential new result. Among samples lacking TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status, PTEN loss has signed estimates of +0.260 [0.182, 0.338] in discovery and +0.275 [0.154, 0.397] in independent validation. Both intervals exceed the 0.15 composite-unit threshold in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, with the validation lower bound only narrowly above threshold because the validation interval is intentionally stringent. I therefore accept and close H108 as the cleanest independent confirmation of the moderate PTEN association after removing the largest competing genomic effects. H82 is also resolved: MSI-high status among TP53-intact, KEAP1-intact, SMARCA4-intact cells has discovery +0.745 [0.666, 0.825] and validation +0.779 [0.675, 0.884], both far above threshold; I accept and close H82, indicating that the MSI-high stronger-dependency association is not merely a consequence of co-occurring TP53, KEAP1, or SMARCA4 loss. The formal MSI-high by TP53-loss interaction in H88 is unsupported: the signed discovery estimate was -0.012 [-0.255, 0.231] and validation was -0.139 [-0.495, 0.217], with intervals crossing null and not exceeding the threshold in the registered negative-interaction direction. I reject and close H88. H55, the negative-signed SMARCA4 by adenocarcinoma interaction, is likewise unsupported: signed discovery estimate -0.174 [-0.312, -0.035] and validation estimate -0.084 [-0.281, 0.113]. Although a positive-sign counterpart was discovered in one analysis, its independent interval was not above threshold, so formal lineage-specific heterogeneity should not be claimed; direct SMARCA4 loss within adenocarcinoma remains supported as a subgroup mean difference. The broader supported supplied-dataset findings are now stable. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency, signed +0.829 [0.767, 0.891], and remains strong across batch_a, Avana, KY, adenocarcinoma, high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, and high aneuploidy. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker dependency, signed main +0.810 [0.745, 0.875] and validated +0.788 [0.698, 0.879], also robust across batch_a, libraries, adenocarcinoma, screen quality, Cas9 activity, and high aneuploidy. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger dependency, signed main +0.804 [0.742, 0.867] and validated +0.800 [0.705, 0.895], robust across libraries, adenocarcinoma, clean TP53/KEAP1 states, stemness extremes, high Cas9, elevated mutation burden, and high aneuploidy. MSI-high is associated with much stronger dependency, signed main +0.775 [0.664, 0.885] and validated +0.842 [0.673, 1.010], robust across triple-intact, adenocarcinoma, batch_a, Avana, screen quality, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, and high aneuploidy. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency predictor, main +0.239 [0.145, 0.332] and validated +0.279 [0.138, 0.419], and it is now well confirmed in the quadruple-intact clean stratum. Important negative or unsupported findings include STK11 loss, KRAS mutation, MYC amplification, MTAP loss, ARID1A loss, RB1 loss, SMAD4 loss, BRCA2 loss, PIK3CA mutation, APC mutation, NF1 loss, media serum percentage, and research markers D, E, and F; ERBB2 amplification and BRAF V600E are near-null; EGFR amplification does not support a stronger-dependency effect in the registered direction. Most formal interaction tests are negative, indicating that the accepted predictors are largely additive associations rather than evidence for multiplicative subgroup modification. Remaining uncertainty is mostly precision-limited rather than contradictory: PTEN remains less robust in some direct subgroups such as batch_a, KY, high aneuploidy pending direct testing, and triple-intact high-Cas9; CDKN2A is near threshold and still needs a clean quadruple-intact estimate; several adenocarcinoma amplifier and EMT or hypoxia strata remain untested. The most informative next analyses are the registered clean PTEN-adenocarcinoma refinement and CDKN2A quadruple-intact test, followed by direct PTEN checks in adenocarcinoma and high aneuploidy, Avana-library main-effect scale checks, and adenocarcinoma-specific amplifier associations. All conclusions should remain framed as associations in this supplied dataset, not as causal single-gene knockout effects or claims of external biological generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 9/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

Iteration 9/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Interpret all findings as supplied-dataset associations only, not causal or externally generalizable.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The prior analyses have established a compact set of robust supplied-dataset associations: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associate with weaker dependency, SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high associate with stronger dependency, and PTEN loss has a moderate stronger-dependency association that is best supported in clean co-occurrence-free strata. The next exploration should therefore do two things. First, it should localize the borderline PTEN association within states that could plausibly explain it: screen quality, editing activity, low aneuploidy, faster proliferation, EMT or hypoxia states, PIK3CA co-mutation, and STK11 co-loss. If the clean PTEN estimate remains above the 0.15-unit threshold in high screen quality, high Cas9 activity, low aneuploidy, and fast-growth states, the PTEN association is unlikely to be explained by technical quality, proliferation, or extreme genomic instability. If it collapses in one or more of these strata, then PTEN should be interpreted as less robust and potentially conditional. Second, it should test whether the strongest accepted associations persist in orthogonal biological states. I register direct mean differences for TP53 loss in high hypoxia, KEAP1 loss in high EMT, SMARCA4 loss in high EMT and high hypoxia, and MSI-high in high EMT. These are not claims of interaction yet; they are direct robustness checks. A persistent above-threshold effect supports an additive association across that state, while attenuation or null results would motivate more careful state-specific interpretation. I also register a focused CDKN2A comparison among samples that are intact for the largest predictors and MSI-high and that have lower 9p21 copy number, because CDKN2A and 9p21 loss are biologically related and the prior main CDKN2A estimate is near threshold. A clean 9p21-low estimate above threshold would support treating CDKN2A loss as a meaningful lower-score association; an estimate near or below threshold would leave CDKN2A unresolved rather than accepted. These proposals deliberately avoid repeating the already registered adenocarcinoma amplifier, PTEN adenocarcinoma, PTEN high-aneuploidy, TP53 high-EMT, and KEAP1 high-hypoxia checks, but they complement them. All interpretations remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal knockout effects or externally generalizable biology.","analyze":"I selected twelve existing untested claims that best probe robustness of the accepted predictors and global technical/biological scale effects. H96-H99 test direct TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss associations in median-or-higher screen quality and Cas9-activity strata, addressing whether the largest weaker-dependency signals depend on screen technical quality or editing activity. H103 tests SMARCA4 loss in elevated mutation burden, a key genomic confounding check for the strong stronger-dependency association. H108 tests PTEN loss after excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high, giving a strict co-occurrence-free estimate for the moderate PTEN signal. H114 further tests PTEN loss in a clean TP53-/KEAP1-/SMARCA4-intact high-Cas9 stratum. H109-H112 test TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high in high aneuploidy, checking whether accepted associations survive genome-wide chromosomal instability. H107 provides a Ky-library main-effect technical scale check; a substantial library effect would require caution when interpreting library-specific subgroup results. These requests prioritize direct robustness over new low-power interactions while retaining breadth across accepted large predictors, the borderline PTEN predictor, and a global library shift.","appraise":"The twelve new discovery analyses strongly reinforce the accepted large predictor associations and clarify which technical or biological strata are decisive. TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in both median-or-better screen-quality samples (+0.838 [0.753,0.923]) and median-or-higher Cas9-activity samples (+0.753 [0.659,0.847]). KEAP1 loss likewise remains associated with weaker dependency in high screen-quality samples (+0.772 [0.678,0.866]) and high Cas9-activity samples (+0.711 [0.612,0.810]). SMARCA4 loss remains strongly associated with stronger dependency in elevated mutation-burden samples (+0.847 [0.755,0.939]). Together with earlier batch, library, lineage, Cas9, screen-quality, and mutation-burden checks, these results argue that the largest associations are not artifacts of screen quality, editing activity, mutation burden, or screen batch. High aneuploidy robustness checks are also strong: TP53 loss +0.891 [0.768,1.013], KEAP1 loss +0.875 [0.736,1.015], SMARCA4 loss +0.784 [0.652,0.916], and MSI-high +0.892 [0.669,1.114], although the MSI-high exposed cell is small. Thus, these accepted associations survive the top quartile of genome-wide chromosomal instability. For PTEN loss, the clean quadruple-intact stratum excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high gives +0.260 [0.182,0.338], entirely above the 0.15-unit threshold and the strongest direct PTEN robustness estimate to date. First, I focus on CDKN2A, which has been repeatedly near the 0.15-unit threshold: H118 tests CDKN2A loss after excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high, while H126 tests the biologically related setting of low 9p21 copy number in that same clean state. An above-threshold clean estimate would justify treating CDKN2A as a meaningful predictor, whereas a near-null estimate would keep it unresolved. Second, I target the moderate PTEN loss association with four informative localization checks: H119 tests PTEN loss among adenocarcinoma samples that are quadruple-intact for the largest competing predictors; H113 tests PTEN loss in high aneuploidy, a genome-instability setting where residual confounding is possible; and H124/H125 test PTEN loss in high EMT and high hypoxia states. These are not interaction claims; they are direct subgroup associations that ask whether the moderate PTEN signal survives important biological states. Third, I run direct robustness checks for the largest accepted predictors in orthogonal stress states: H115 for TP53 loss in high EMT, H116 for KEAP1 loss in high hypoxia, H129/H130 for SMARCA4 loss in high EMT and high hypoxia, and H131 for MSI-high in high EMT. Persistent above-threshold effects would support additive associations across those states; attenuation would motivate more conditional interpretation. Iteration 9/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative:
The new discovery results largely reinforce the robustness of the accepted large predictors and clarify which moderate or borderline associations remain precision-limited. In orthogonal biological stress states, TP53 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in high EMT (+0.832 [0.718, 0.946]), KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker dependency in high hypoxia (+0.800 [0.677, 0.924]), SMARCA4 loss remains associated with stronger dependency in high EMT (+0.763 [0.634, 0.893]) and high hypoxia (+0.848 [0.725, 0.971]), and MSI-high remains associated with stronger dependency in high EMT (+0.610 [0.413, 0.808]). These intervals are entirely above the 0.15-unit threshold, so I accept and close these subgroup robustness checks. The MSI-high high-EMT estimate uses a small exposed cell, but even the 95% lower bound exceeds threshold, so the association is supported in this dataset.

For PTEN loss, the moderate stronger-dependency signal is again localized in a biologically clean adenocarcinoma stratum. After excluding TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high status, PTEN loss among adenocarcinomas has signed estimate +0.279 [0.186, 0.373], entirely above threshold. This is a meaningful refinement of the already validated general PTEN and clean-quadruple-intact PTEN associations, so I accept H119 and request validation as the most informative remaining PTEN claim. In contrast, direct high-aneuploidy PTEN (+0.271 [0.087, 0.455]), high-EMT PTEN (+0.328 [0.143, 0.513]), and high-hypoxia PTEN (+0.261 [0.087, 0.435]) have point estimates above threshold but lower bounds below threshold. I leave them unresolved and deferred rather than accepting them as independent evidence, because the uncertainty does not exclude differences smaller than the scientifically meaningful threshold.

CDKN2A remains unresolved. In the quadruple-intact clean stratum, the signed estimate is +0.148 [0.093, 0.204], slightly below threshold; in the clean low-9p21 refinement it is +0.151 [0.090, 0.212], barely above threshold but with a lower bound below threshold. These results do not justify accepting CDKN2A as a meaningful predictor, but they are not clearly null, so I defer them.
