record.narrative:
The response deadline for H94 (PTEN loss in batch_a) is now met. Discovery was positive but not fully above the 0.15-unit threshold: R84 gave +0.258 with 95% interval [0.063, 0.454]. The independent validation is weaker and not confirmatory: R93 gave +0.190 with an independent interval [-0.061, 0.440]. Because the validation lower bound crosses both the threshold and null, I cannot call PTEN loss a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency effect in batch_a. I do not mark it as a strict negative finding because the upper bound remains compatible with a large effect; instead, I leave it unresolved but close this particular subgroup as precision-limited and not useful for further validation. This refines the PTEN picture: the clean, low-confounding PTEN association is now well supported, while the direct batch_a subgroup is not independently supported.

H119 is decisively resolved. PTEN loss in adenocarcinoma samples that are intact for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high was +0.279 [0.186, 0.373] in discovery and +0.289 [0.158, 0.420] in independent validation. Both lower bounds exceed the 0.15 composite-unit threshold in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, although the validation lower bound is only modestly above threshold. I accept and close H119. Together with H44, H49, and H108, this gives a coherent PTEN pattern: PTEN loss is associated with moderately stronger dependency, most reproducibly when competing large genomic associations are removed, and especially in adenocarcinoma. It is not uniformly confirmed in every direct stress, instability, or batch subgroup.

The broader scientific picture remains a compact set of supplied-dataset associations, not causal single-gene effects. TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are robustly associated with weaker dependency, with signed effects around +0.83 and +0.81 and reproducibility across libraries, batches, lineage, screen quality, Cas9 activity, aneuploidy, and stress-state strata. SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger dependency, with signed main effects around +0.80 and +0.78 and independent validation above threshold. PTEN loss is a moderate, validated stronger-dependency association, best established in clean quadruple-intact and clean adenocarcinoma settings. Many other measured predictors are unsupported or near-null, including STK11, KRAS, MYC, MTAP, ARID1A, RB1, SMAD4, BRCA2, PIK3CA, APC, NF1, media serum percentage, research markers D/E/F, EGFR amplification in adenocarcinoma, and prior EGFR/ERBB2/BRAF global checks. Formal interactions are mostly negative, so the accepted effects are best described as largely additive associations in this dataset rather than strong effect modification.

The main unresolved uncertainty is CDKN2A and residual PTEN localization. CDKN2A loss repeatedly sits near the 0.15-unit threshold: quadruple-intact +0.148 [0.093, 0.204] and clean low-9p21 +0.151 [0.090, 0.212]. These are not acceptable as meaningful differences because their lower bounds fall below threshold, but they are also not clearly null. For PTEN, direct high-EMT, high-hypoxia, high-aneuploidy, KY, and batch_a checks are either unresolved or unsupported; the next best analyses are clean, confounder-free versions of the stress-state and quality checks, plus high-quality CDKN2A checks. I therefore register refinements for CDKN2A in high-quality clean strata and for PTEN in clean high-EMT, clean high-hypoxia, and clean adenocarcinoma high-quality strata. These should determine whether the moderate CDKN2A/PTEN signals can be separated from technical and biological context, while the existing active PTEN clean screen-quality, Cas9, aneuploidy, growth-rate, PIK3CA, and STK11 checks remain reasonable follow-ups. Amplifier checks in adenocarcinoma are lower priority and are deferred because the accepted predictor set is already concentrated on genomic-loss, MSI, and PTEN biology.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

I leave them unresolved and deferred rather than accepting them as independent evidence, because the uncertainty does not exclude differences smaller than the scientifically meaningful threshold.\n\nCDKN2A remains unresolved. In the quadruple-intact clean stratum, the signed estimate is +0.148 [0.093, 0.204], slightly below threshold; in the clean low-9p21 refinement it is +0.151 [0.090, 0.212], barely above threshold but with a lower bound below threshold. Discovery was positive but not fully above the 0.15-unit threshold: R84 gave +0.258 with 95% interval [0.063, 0.454]. The independent validation is weaker and not confirmatory: R93 gave +0.190 with an independent interval [-0.061, 0.440]. Because the validation lower bound crosses both the threshold and null, I cannot call PTEN loss a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency effect in batch_a. I do not mark it as a strict negative finding because the upper bound remains compatible with a large effect; instead, I leave it unresolved but close this particular subgroup as precision-limited and not useful for further validation. This refines the PTEN picture: the clean, low-confounding PTEN association is now well supported, while the direct batch_a subgroup is not independently supported.\n\nH119 is decisively resolved. PTEN loss in adenocarcinoma samples that are intact for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high was +0.279 [0.186, 0.373] in discovery and +0.289 [0.158, 0.420] in independent validation. Both lower bounds exceed the 0.15 composite-unit threshold in the claimed stronger-dependency direction, although the validation lower bound is only modestly above threshold. I accept and close H119. Together with H44, H49, and H108, this gives a coherent PTEN pattern: PTEN loss is associated with moderately stronger dependency, most reproducibly when competing large genomic associations are removed, and especially in adenocarcinoma. It is not uniformly confirmed in every direct stress, instability, or batch subgroup.\n\nThe broader scientific picture remains a compact set of supplied-dataset associations, not causal single-gene effects. TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are robustly associated with weaker dependency, with signed effects around +0.83 and +0.81 and reproducibility across libraries, batches, lineage, screen quality, Cas9 activity, aneuploidy, and stress-state strata. SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are robustly associated with stronger dependency, with signed main effects around +0.80 and +0.78 and independent validation above threshold. PTEN loss is a moderate, validated stronger-dependency association, best established in clean quadruple-intact and clean adenocarcinoma settings. CDKN2A loss repeatedly sits near the 0.15-unit threshold: quadruple-intact +0.148 [0.093, 0.204] and clean low-9p21 +0.151 [0.090, 0.212]. These are not acceptable as meaningful differences because their lower bounds fall below threshold, but they are also not clearly null. record.narrative: The accepted predictor set is stable, so the next comparisons should mainly resolve the two open issues: (1) whether CDKN2A loss is a meaningful predictor or only a borderline association, and (2) whether the moderate PTEN stronger-dependency association survives technical-quality, adenocarcinoma, high-mutation-burden, and slow-growth contexts when competing large effects are removed. I therefore register clean quadruple-intact CDKN2A comparisons in low aneuploidy, high screen quality with high Cas9 activity, and high mutation burden. For PTEN, I register clean comparisons in combined high screen quality/high Cas9 activity, clean adenocarcinoma with high Cas9, clean high mutation burden, and clean slow-growth samples. These are direct subgroup mean differences, not formal interaction claims, and they test whether the moderate PTEN effect is robust rather than confined to permissive quality or proliferation states. I also register robustness checks for the large accepted predictors in orthogonal genomic contexts: TP53 and KEAP1 in high mutation burden and low aneuploidy, and SMARCA4 in low aneuploidy. A persistent above-threshold signed effect in these strata would support broad supplied-dataset additivity; attenuation or nullity would motivate a more conditional interpretation. All claims remain dataset associations, not causal knockout effects or externally generalizable biology.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Iteration 10/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new discovery set does not change the established supplied-dataset associations for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, or broadly validated PTEN loss. It mainly refines the borderline CDKN2A question and the localization of the moderate PTEN stronger-dependency signal. For CDKN2A loss in clean quadruple-intact strata, the signed estimates are near the 0.15 composite-unit threshold and precision is limited: high screen quality gives +0.189 with lower bound +0.099 (H134), high mutation burden gives +0.163 with lower bound +0.087 (H141), and the high-quality intersection gives only +0.151 with lower bound +0.022 (H140). High Cas9 gives +0.120 (H135), and low aneuploidy gives +0.088 with a lower bound crossing zero (H139). These results are compatible with a weak-to-borderline association but do not provide precise support for a scientifically meaningful effect above the threshold. I keep H134 and H141 active unresolved, defer H140 because of small cell sizes, and close H135 and H139 as not useful independent evidence. For PTEN loss, the clean high-quality and clean stress-state checks mostly have point estimates above threshold, but the intervals are imprecise enough that lower bounds fall below threshold in several strata: clean high screen +0.253 [0.146,0.360] (H120), clean high Cas9 +0.243 [0.130,0.355] (H121), clean high hypoxia +0.297 [0.149,0.446] (H137), and clean high mutation burden +0.220 [0.097,0.343] (H144). The clean high EMT, clean adenocarcinoma high-screen, and clean adenocarcinoma high-Cas9 checks have wider intervals or smaller exposed cells: H136 +0.219 [0.049,0.389], H138 +0.244 [0.126,0.363], and H143 +0.267 [0.126,0.409]. These are supportive of the already accepted PTEN pattern, especially after H44, H49, H108, and H119, but they are not decisive enough for independent subgroup acceptance at the threshold. I defer H120, H121, and H144, keep the closest clean high-hypoxia check active, and close the wider or redundant adenocarcinoma high-quality checks. From a critical-reviewer standpoint, these are multiplicity-prone subgroup analyses with several small exposed cells and potential residual confounding by unmeasured genomic context, so accepting borderline lower bounds would overstate the evidence. I do not request the remaining validation now because none of the new claims has a two-sided 95% discovery interval entirely above the 0.15 threshold, and validation intervals are more stringent; a validation request would be better reserved for a future claim that becomes decisively above threshold. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 10/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: H108's validation deadline is met. PTEN loss in the clean quadruple-intact stratum remains decisively supported: discovery R100 is +0.260 [0.182, 0.338] and independent validation R106 is +0.275 [0.154, 0.397], both signed in the claimed stronger-dependency direction and both entirely above the 0.15-unit threshold even under the stricter validation interval. This strengthens the PTEN association in the low-confounding setting and complements H49/H119. It is still only an association in this supplied dataset, not causal evidence or external generalizability. H88's validation deadline is also met, but does not support effect modification. The discovery interaction R71 was -0.012 [-0.255, 0.231] and independent validation R107 is -0.139 [-0.495, 0.217]. Although the validation point is more in the claimed direction, its wide interval includes both null and the threshold region, so there is no evidence that TP53 loss materially modifies the MSI-high dependency association. I therefore reject the H88 interaction claim and close it; this is rejection of a claimed effect modification, not proof of exact equality. Overall, the compact supplied-dataset model remains largely additive: TP53 and KEAP1 loss associate with weaker dependency, SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high with stronger dependency, and PTEN loss with moderate stronger dependency, best established after removing competing large effects. CDKN2A remains borderline unresolved: several clean strata hover near 0.15 but have lower bounds below threshold. No new validation request is warranted now because none of the new or active borderline subgroup estimates has an interval decisively above threshold, and independent validation intervals are more stringent. Next priority is to finish broad robustness checks for the accepted predictors and only revisit CDKN2A/PTEN localization if an analysis yields an interval clearly crossing threshold.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. The accepted supplied-dataset predictor set is already broad, so this round targets two remaining robustness questions and one technical coverage gap. First, screen_doubling_time_hours is lower for faster growth, so I use <=52 hours as a faster-or-median growth context. I ask whether the accepted TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high associations remain signed in the same direction and remain scientifically meaningful in faster/median doubling contexts. Plausible alternatives include attenuation, reversal, or nullity if growth rate changes pathway dependencies. For PTEN loss, I register a cleaner faster-growth estimate after removing the four largest competing predictors, and a formal faster-vs-slower interaction within the same clean quadruple-intact eligible population. The primary scientific expectation for the interaction is approximate additivity, but the claimed direction is set negative to test the plausible alternative that PTEN loss has a stronger dependency effect in faster/median-growth than slower-growth contexts; anticipated_direction is therefore zero. Second, I register adenocarcinoma estimates for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high after removing the other large predictors, to check whether accepted effects are not merely subtype-mix or co-occurrence artifacts. Finally, crispr_library_humagne_cd is the remaining untested library indicator; its main effect tests residual platform association, with no strong biological expectation. All comparisons remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal knockout effects or externally generalizable claims. No validation is requested at this stage.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. H156 asks a new PTEN growth-rate modification question: within the clean quadruple-intact population, whether the PTEN-loss stronger-dependency contrast differs in faster/median versus slower/missing doubling cells. Library main-effect checks such as H117 and H161 are deferred because biological predictor robustness is more informative under the 12-analysis limit. record.narrative:
The newly delivered comparisons strongly support the same supplied-dataset association pattern rather than creating contradictions. In lower-aneuploidy cells, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and SMARCA4 loss all remain far above the 0.15-unit absolute threshold, with signed intervals [0.600,0.866], [0.598,0.847], and [0.601,0.861] respectively in their claimed directions. This is compatible with modest attenuation relative to some higher-aneuploidy estimates, but all intervals are wide and overlapping, and no formal aneuploidy-by-predictor interaction was tested; therefore I interpret these as robustness checks, not evidence of aneuploidy modification. In faster-or-median doubling contexts (screen doubling time <=52 hours), TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and MSI-high also remain decisively beyond threshold: signed estimates are +0.863, +0.794, +0.766, and +0.820, with all intervals above 0.15 in the claimed direction. The clean adenocarcinoma comparisons, which additionally exclude TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, or MSI-high confounders for each focal predictor, are also all decisive: TP53 +0.791, KEAP1 +0.788, SMARCA4 +0.792, and MSI-high +0.720, each interval entirely above threshold. These clean-context estimates reduce concern that the focal predictors are merely proxies for co-occurring large predictors or subtype mix, although they remain observational associations rather than causal knockout effects.

The only new claim that does not support a scientifically meaningful modification is H156, the PTEN-loss interaction comparing faster/median versus slower/observed-growth cells after excluding the four large competing predictors. Its signed estimate is essentially null (-0.017) and its interval spans both null and opposite-direction values. I reject this interaction claim as unsupported, but this is not proof of exact absence of modification. It also depends on observed screen_doubling_time, so missing growth-rate values could introduce selection bias; this makes it especially unsuitable to overinterpret. Given the multiplicity of subgroup analyses, the decisive large effects for the four main predictors are reassuring, while H156 is treated as a failed interaction check. I request independent validation of H159 because it is a clean adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss context after removing the three other large predictors, filling a useful independent gap for subtype specificity and co-occurrence independence. All conclusions remain limited to this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 11/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: I accept H119 and H159 with closed investigation. H119 tests PTEN-loss association in a clean quadruple-intact adenocarcinoma stratum excluding TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, and MSI-high. The signed estimate remains in the stronger-dependency direction: discovery R112 is +0.279 [0.186,0.373] and independent validation R120 is +0.289 [0.158,0.420]. The validation lower bound is only modestly above the 0.15-unit threshold, but it is still beyond threshold under the stricter validation interval, and the point estimate is stable. I therefore accept this as a supported supplied-dataset association in the low-confounding adenocarcinoma setting. H159 tests SMARCA4-loss association in clean adenocarcinoma excluding competing large predictors. Discovery R143 is +0.792 [0.746,0.837] and independent validation R145 is +0.759 [0.691,0.827], both signed in the claimed stronger-dependency direction and decisively beyond threshold. This strongly supports SMARCA4-loss dependency association in a clean subtype-relevant context. Overall, the compact evidence-supported model remains largely additive and consistent: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associate with weaker dependency, while SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, and PTEN loss associate with stronger dependency. The strongest validated predictors are TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN in clean or independently validated strata. The next most informative step is formal testing of high-versus-nonhigh aneuploidy interactions for these accepted predictors. Subgroup main effects in high and low aneuploidy suggest possible magnitude differences, especially for TP53 and KEAP1, but no formal interaction has yet shown decisive modification. I registered formal high-aneuploidy interaction tests for TP53, KEAP1, SMARCA4, MSI-high, and PTEN. If these remain null, the additive model is preferred; if a signed interval decisively exceeds threshold, the relevant context should be refined. CDKN2A remains borderline and should not be accepted unless a future interval has lower bound above 0.15 in the claimed direction. All conclusions remain observational associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum

record.narrative: No assessments are due. The accepted supplied-dataset association model remains additive: TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss associate with weaker dependency, while SMARCA4 loss, MSI-high, and PTEN loss associate with stronger dependency. The next high-value step is to test whether the strongest predictors are modified by measured tumor-microenvironment-like contexts, especially hypoxia, rather than relying only on main effects within contexts. I register formal interactions for TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and a clean-context PTEN-loss estimate under high hypoxia. The claim directions follow the accepted main effects, so a positive interval in the claimed direction would mean the predictor is especially associated with its accepted dependency pattern in high-hypoxia cells relative to lower-hypoxia cells. The scientific alternative is approximate additivity or attenuation. For PTEN loss, I also propose a refinement of the earlier PTEN-by-PIK3CA interaction within MSI-negative cells. The prior biological hypothesis is that PTEN/PI3K pathway co-perturbation may produce a larger dependency association, but the original H52 interval was not decisive. Restricting to MSI-negative cells reduces the strongest alternative confounder while preserving cell sizes, making this a useful focused follow-up. I reassess H52 as unresolved but closed because it is superseded by the MSI-negative refinement. I close the two remaining library main-effect checks, H117 and H161, as low-priority technical coverage; library robustness has already been broadly demonstrated across Avana and KY contexts, and the remaining analysis slots are better allocated to biological context interactions. All proposed claims are supplied-dataset associations; they do not establish causality or generalizability. Validation requests are exhausted, so conclusions will rely on discovery precision, pre-registered directions, and the existing validated anchors.

prompt:
Iteration 12/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
